title: Sanofi Reports Q3 and Labor-Cost Data Hit at 8:30 A.M. as Markets Open Lower
dek: Sanofi's third-quarter webcast and the government's Employment Cost Index both land at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, just as tech futures slide.
author: Meridian Newsroom

keyPoints: Sanofi reports third-quarter 2026 results with a live webcast at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on October 30 (Sanofi).
Analysts polled by MarketBeat expect earnings of $1.63 a share for the quarter.
The BLS releases the third-quarter Employment Cost Index at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on October 30 (BLS).
The second-quarter ECI rose 0.9% for the quarter and 3.4% over the year for civilian workers (BLS).
body:
## Two 8:30 a.m. events

Two scheduled releases land at 8:30 a.m. Eastern this morning, just as premarket trading turns lower. The first is Sanofi's third-quarter 2026 results. Sanofi says management will review the quarter in a live audio webcast at 8:30 a.m. Eastern (13:30 to 14:30 CET) on October 30, followed by a question-and-answer session ([Sanofi investor relations](https://www.sanofi.com/en/investors/financial-results-and-events/financial-results)). The second is the Employment Cost Index for the third quarter, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics schedules for 8:30 a.m. Eastern on the same day ([Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/eci/)).

## Sanofi: the consensus bar

MarketBeat reports analysts expect Sanofi to report third-quarter earnings of $1.63 a share before the market opens ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-sanofi-sny-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-friday-2026-10-23/)). That figure is a consensus estimate, not a company guide. Sanofi's own investor page describes the quarter's focus areas as immunology, rare diseases and vaccines, with a continued push to rebuild the pipeline through business development and deals. Investors will be listening for how management addresses that pipeline, since the company has signaled that acquisitions are part of its plan.

For U.S. investors, Sanofi's stock trades as an American depositary receipt under SNY. A clean beat on earnings would help defensive healthcare names in a session where tech is weak. A miss, or a change in guidance, would add to pressure on the sector.

## The labor-cost read

The Employment Cost Index measures the change in what employers pay for labor, including wages and benefits, and it is watched closely by the Federal Reserve for signs of services inflation. The second-quarter reading showed civilian compensation up 0.9% over the quarter and 3.4% over the year. Private-industry compensation rose 0.9% in the quarter.

A hotter-than-expected third-quarter print would reinforce the view that labor costs are not easing quickly, at a time when oil is rising. WTI crude was up about 2% in premarket trading. That combination is what makes the 8:30 a.m. data relevant to rate expectations, not just to the labor market.

## How it could move markets

The ECI is most likely to matter for Treasury yields and rate-sensitive stocks in the first hour. Sanofi's result is more likely to matter for its own stock and for the healthcare sector. Confidence is medium on the ECI effect, because the market reaction depends on the surprise versus consensus, which this article does not have. Confidence is low on Sanofi's direction until the release is out.

## What is not yet known

At the time of writing, this article does not have Sanofi's actual third-quarter figures or the ECI result. Both will be added in the midday update once the releases are verified.

marketImpact.summary: Two 8:30 a.m. releases give the open a catalyst: Sanofi's quarter, which matters for healthcare and its ADR, and the ECI, which matters for rate expectations and Treasury yields.

tickers.rationale: Results against a $1.63 consensus EPS estimate; direction depends on the surprise and guidance
A hotter labor-cost print would push yields higher and weigh on long-duration bonds
